_README: Example managed settings for an organisation deploying ai-native-sdlc.
Managed settings are deployed by the platform team through MDM or the admin
console. They sit ABOVE every other settings layer, and an engineer cannot
override them. That is what makes this file — not the plugin — the layer
that decides whether the gates are negotiable.
Do not copy this verbatim. Every deny rule removes a capability, and the
right balance depends on the data classification of the repositories it
covers. Start from it, then argue each line.
THE LINE THAT MATTERS MOST is enabledPlugins. With allowManagedHooksOnly
set and this plugin NOT force-enabled there, every hook it ships is
silently blocked and the plugin looks installed while enforcing nothing.
NOTE on sandbox.failIfUnavailable: it is false here on purpose. OS-level
sandboxing is unsupported on native Windows, so setting it true would stop
Claude Code starting at all for every Windows engineer. Set it to true only
for a fleet that is entirely macOS, Linux or WSL2 — and understand that on
Windows this plugin's hooks are then the ONLY enforcement layer, which is
why its safety-critical gates fail closed rather than open.
